description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 at 8de517a28 (coordinator probe, cargo test --lib):
    meters <: int = false     int <: meters = true
    utf8   <: bin = false     bin <: utf8   = true
    display(mint_brand(int, "Meters")) = "int | Meters"
.agent/docs/set-theoretic-types.md:219-240 states the law the other way:
"`utf8 <: binary` because dropping the `brands` axis leaves a structural
`binary`, while a plain `binary` is not a `utf8` because the unbranded type
lacks the tag" -- a brand is a NOMINAL REFINEMENT of its inner, i.e. a
SUBTYPE. The code does the opposite: mint_brand (types/mod.rs:645) clones
the inner's Descr and sets brands = {name}; an unbranded Descr carries brands
= none() (descr.rs:63) and the subtype relation compares the brands axis as
a set, so the empty brands set is inside every singleton and the branded
type becomes the SUPERTYPE (the display renders it as a union). Every
consumer of the lattice inherits the inversion: a @spec position declared
`integer` rejects a Meters argument and accepts a bare int at a Meters
position; today the pattern-derived witness (fz-kdt.192's subject) hides the
rejection at spec positions by accident, and fz-kdt.192 makes it reachable
(probe X5: `({int, a}) :: a` at {Meters, int} -> Invalid). Corpus: 0 movers
(no fixture passes a branded value to a ground-inner spec position) -- which
also means the brand model has no behavioural gate in the corpus.
FIX (data-model up): the brands axis of an UNBRANDED type must denote "no
constraint" (top on that axis) and a brand a finite refinement, so that A <:
B iff structure(A) ⊆ structure(B) and (B unbranded or brands(A) ⊆
brands(B)); erase_nominal (descr.rs:525-541) and the cofinite-brands branch
must be re-derived with it; display must not render a refinement as a union.
Red-first: the four probe lines above as unit pins of the DOCUMENTED law
(meters <: int, not int <: meters; utf8 <: bin); a three-door fixture that
passes a branded value to an inner-typed @spec and to a brand-typed @spec
(the latter rejecting a bare inner) with an Elixir oracle for the values
(brands are runtime-erased, fz-bsx). CONCORDANCE: fz-bsx (the brand model:
runtime brand-blind, typing brand-aware), fz-kdt.169/172/173 (closure
brands -- a different axis, untouched), fz-kdt.192 (which this BLOCKS: a
witness that is the raw argument must not reject what the law admits).

comments.text: RESEARCH DONE, PROTOTYPED (2026-09-03, proto198.diff, being cold-reviewed). THE ENCODING: brands is a conjunctive REFINEMENT FACTOR over all kind axes -- a Descr denotes S x B with `unbranded` an element every cofinite FiniteSet contains and no finite one names (finite_set.rs unchanged); unbranded int = brands any(), mint_brand = brands {Meters}; Descr::none() keeps brands none() (the union identity), NEW Descr::unbranded() is every value constructor's base (13 constructors re-based; six sites built from none() had silently become the empty type -- two in canon.rs saturate/absorb saturated every DNF axis to top); intersect pointwise (Meters ∧ Feet = ∅: ONE BRAND PER VALUE), diff factor-wise and exact for the three brand shapes, negation two rectangles (Descr::neg now test-only), erase_nominal = brands any() (cofinite branch deleted), display renders a refinement: utf8(binary), not(Meters)(int). Deleted: brand_of at three layers. MEASURED: 13 unit pins red at HEAD / green; lib 1626/0/5; matrix HEAD 485/6/9 (six new brand trials) -> 491/0/9; corpus interp/run/canon 0 movers, executables 5297; the live defect: M.echo(binary) with a utf8 value -> spec/violation at HEAD, "hi" fixed; Utf8.to_bytes(utf8) with a bare binary -> accepted at HEAD, spec/violation fixed (two new three-door fixtures). RESIDUE: a union of brands over DIFFERENT inners loses the pairing (needs a union of rectangles; unreachable: no program has two brands). OWNER QUESTIONS: (1) is one brand per value the model? (2) `int` = "int, branded or not" -- a bare int is not writable in source. (3) THERE IS NO USER-LEVEL WAY TO MINT A BRANDED VALUE: `@type Meters :: refines integer` declares the type but every body producing one returns a bare int, which the argument gate then rejects at any Meters position; utf8 works only because an extern returns any and the return side is unchecked (fz-kdt.201). A minting form (Meters.new/1, an `as` cast, or `refines` publishing a constructor) is a prerequisite for user brands to be usable at all.

title: [BUG] The brand lattice is inverted: is_subtype(mint_brand(int, "Meters"), int) is false and is_subtype(int, Meters) is true, contradicting set-theoretic-types.md's law `utf8 <: binary`
